h: לְרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ מְנַחֵם אָב, ה׳ Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av, 5

p: [מִשְׁנַת חֲסִידִים, מַסֶּכֶת תַּמּוּז וְאָב, פֶּרֶק ב]
that on this Rosh Chodesh one should have in mind
out of the twelve combinations of the Name
that emerges from the initial letters of the verse
"Haskeis u'shma Yisrael hayom" — "Pay attention and hear, Yisrael, today."
the holiness of the month of Av
Now, the order of the Name Havayah,
when it is in its regular order,
as it emerges from the initials of the verse
"Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad" —
it is known that it alludes:
and the first Hei the aspect of Imma;
as is known from the holy Zohar
And in the combination of this month
the Yud is between the letters Vav and Hei.
The point is that the Vav, as is known,
that runs from end to end" —
that is, from the letter Yud,
which is the aspect of Chochmah,
which alludes to Ayin, Kesser Elyon,
it bestows down to the lower Hei,
Now, there is an upper Yud,
which alludes to the lower Chochmah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רטו, ב)
from within the holy upper Yud."
the Yud comes after the Vav,
which is the attribute of Malchus;
and it alludes to the day of Shabbos,
the word "hayom" — as referring to the day of Shabbos,
that the three Shabbos meals are derived
and likewise it is expounded (Shocher Tov, Tehillim 95):
"Today, if you will listen to His voice"
as referring to the day of Shabbos:
that if they keep one Shabbos,
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינָן לָהּ
"the mouth: we call it Torah she'b'al peh"
And the letter Vav is the letter of truth
meaning that all of Torah she'b'al peh
is alluded to in Torah she'b'chsav.
is the aspect of Ruach HaKodesh,
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג סא, א)
and in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 61a):
that is to say, a spirit from that supernal 'Kodesh.'"
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א מז, ב)
וְזֶה הוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And this is what is said in the holy Zohar
and because Shabbos is called speech,"
And this is along the lines of what is expounded
"A young Torah scholar who flares up —
it is the Torah that makes him flare up,
And this is along the lines of what it says
"My words which I have placed in your mouth."
that in the combination of this month
between the letters Vav and Hei,
which alludes to the lower Yud,
the aspect of the wisdom of Shlomo,
which emerges from within the upper Yud,
which is the utterance "Let there be light,"
corresponding to the five books of the Torah
together with the tip of the Yud,
which is the light hidden away for the tzaddikim
And this is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
which comes from the dew of Atika,
"My utterance shall flow like the dew."
of this combination to this month,
in which, because of our sins,
the Beis HaMikdash and Yerushalayim were destroyed;
"For from Tziyon will go forth Torah,
and the word of Hashem from Yerushalayim";
of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
"from which Torah goes forth to all Yisrael."
and spread of Torah she'b'al peh
when the Torah was forgotten from Yisrael,
"Ezra came up from Bavel and re-established it," and so on;
"Hillel the Babylonian came up and re-established it," and so on;
"Rabbi Chiya and his sons came up and re-established it."
the Men of the Great Assembly,
Knesses Yisrael is called by the name Tziyon,
"the spreading of the shelter of peace,"
and "Yisrael are called by the name of Tziyon,
'And to say to Tziyon, You are My people'"
And the main purpose of the length of the exile
is to merit the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
"And You give life to them all"
(and this has been explained many times).
And this is the holiness of the month of Av,
to merit the light of Torah she'b'al peh
which is the Yud with its tip,
which alludes to the hidden light.
הוּא בְּרָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת שֶׁל תֵּיבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
is at the head of the word "Yisrael";
and with men, and you have prevailed"
That is, through the spreading forth
which receives from the dew of Atika,
there is the abundance of wisdom
to rectify the abundance of anger;
and this is the Torah she'b'al peh,
And Shabbos is designated for this:
and to break the yetzer hara
are likened to Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג כט, ב),
and they merit Torah she'b'al peh,
whose source is from Tziyon and Yerushalayim,
